method.name: controlBridge
method.signature: controlBridge(command: { kind: 'send'; transportId: string; request: IpcBridgeRequest } | { kind: 'cancel'; transportId: string }): AsyncIterable<{ transportId: string; kind: 'written' | 'cancelled' | 'frame' | 'closed' | 'error'; written?: boolean; frame?: string; code?: string }>;
method.purpose: The additive sc6 controlBridge envelope preserves existing inner frame types. Launch the helper explicitly in bridge-control protocol 2 and require version confirmation before sending; mismatch fails with no legacy fallback. Each send/cancel/event has a unique transportId bound to its embedded RPC request id and lane, never reused during helper lifetime. Validate before queue admission. A cancel processed before the first named-pipe write attempt removes the send, confirms cancelled/written=false and forbids later dispatch. At the first write attempt, mark written=true conservatively: possible dispatch, not application completion. A helper-stdin write is not pipe dispatch evidence. Post-write cancellation retires the local reply without rollback/replay promises. Helper death/lost outcome leaves unresolved sends unknown unless not-written was positively confirmed. Frame/error/close events carry transportId; report every pending id on lane failure where possible. Preserve 64-pending/16MiB aggregate bounds, fragmented UTF-8 and separate stream-lane cancellation. Input EOF closes the helper lane, never daemon.

body.rationale: Provide correlated cancellation/write outcomes for multiplexed Windows bridge lanes without changing application RPC frames.
